Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The text describes two distinct proteomics efforts: 1) a TMT-based analysis of biochemically active fractions (PXD028832) and 2) a FLAG-IP based identification of binding partners (PXD029574). Both used DDA. The primary routing for the PRIDE metadata provided is AP-MS.

scope: FLAG-tagged METTL5 was expressed in Freestyle 293 cells and pulled down with anti-FLAG-M2 antibody-coupled magnetic beads. Bound proteins were fractionated by SDS-PAGE, and bands of interest were cut out for proteomics analysis.

In total, 500 μl FLAG-M2 magnetic beads (Sigma) were washed three times with 2 ml lysis buffer per wash and added to lysate and rotated for 30 min at 4 °C. ... Bound proteins were then eluted with 500uL of 2x Laemmli sample buffer (BioRad) supplemented with 100 mM DTT by heating at 70 °C for 15 min, shaking at 1000 rpm. Samples were then separated on a 4 to 12% bis-tris gradient gel and stained by Silver Stain for Mass Spectrometry (Pierce). Bands of interest were excised using razor blades and stored in 1.5 ml tubes at −80 °C prior to being shipped on dry ice and analyzed by MS BioWorks, LLC (Band ID service).

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics experiment described in the PRIDE metadata and the 'METTL5 binding partner ID' section specifically analyzed proteins affinity-purified via FLAG-tagged METTL5. While the text mentions a separate TMT analysis of 'HeLa nuclear extract' (PXD028832), the primary focus of the provided PRIDE metadata (PXD029574) is the affinity purification of the METTL5 complex.
